profile.name: Barbarian
profile.accent: Broad, hearty Northern English, as heard in Yorkshire.
profile.style: A restless undead thing dragged back from the grave. Hollow, breathy, and sepulchral, the voice echoing as if from a long way off. A lingering, sorrowful spirit. Wispy, far-off, and forlorn, half-faded from the world of the living. A boisterous barbarian of the wilds. Loud, blunt, and full-blooded, proud of strength and scornful of soft folk.
profile.pace: Forceful and robust, full of gusto.

profile.name: Miner (Motherlode Mine)
profile.accent: Gruff Scottish English, as heard in Glasgow.
profile.style: A stout, hard-bitten mountain dwarf. Rough, gravelly, and blunt, with the no-nonsense grit of a lifetime at the forge. A gruff, hard-working dwarven miner; terse, weary and down-to-earth.
profile.pace: Firm and forthright, clipped and a little impatient.

profile.name: Murphy
profile.accent: A Liverpudlian accent, the distinctive Scouse sound of Merseyside in northern England, for the folk of Kandarin.
profile.style: An ordinary citizen of Gielinor. Down-to-earth, sincere, and approachable. A weather-beaten seafarer who has spent too long dealing with rough crews and rougher water, practical, sturdy, and only mildly patient.
